title: R4A Authoring entrypoint convergence
summary: Exact R4A proposal approved by user; execute 24 ordered slices and conditional material-visual checkpoint.

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.

allowedWork: s01: Pin the two author tasks, owner/host/capability map, output baselines and command names; reconcile stale workflow summary; risk Low; F: exact arithmetic, source/host refs, clean baseline; one commit.
s02: Register real consumer cost fixtures and measure import/inference costs before designing shared exports; risk Medium; S: unchanged fixtures/ceilings; negative type cases; one commit.

s03: Derive the bounded task/capability inventory from existing owners; distinguish check, preview, extraction and publication; risk Medium; S: coverage matches executed capabilities; unknown task negatives; one commit.

s04: Define the smallest reporting adapter over existing results; preserve domain diagnostics and source authority; risk Medium; S: exhaustive success/gap cases, no forged prepared/publication states; one commit.
s05: Add explicit read-only example/check dispatch with exact task selection and lazy owner loading; risk Medium; B: invalid selection, missing source, size limits, import isolation; one commit.

s06: Route Bayes through its existing checker; preserve both input forms, zero-condition gaps and revision pins; risk Medium; S: old/new invocation equivalence and complete failure payloads; one commit.

s07: Expose the existing numeric equation draft compilation through the same domain-owned boundary used by the browser; risk High; B: numeric domain restrictions, exact endpoints, forged source rejection; one commit.
s08: Make the selected equation CLI path use that boundary; retain the explicitly pinned legacy example contract; risk Medium; S: reference and numeric variants, narration, typed repairs; one commit.

s09: Align existing browser preparation with the shared domain boundary without changing Apply or playback ownership; risk High; B + V: last-valid, stale preparation, atomic count/text/ink, reverse and interruption; one commit.
s10: Run the two primary author workflows end to end and produce a compact comparison packet; risk Medium; V: real CLI-to-existing-editor-to-local-edition exercise; one commit.
s11: Route existing reusable equation reasoning through its owner; preserve assumptions, extraction and exact return; risk Medium; S + V: source/revision/prompt parity and return address; one commit.

s12: Pressure the reporting/dispatch seam with existing code reasoning without claiming arbitrary-source generation; risk High; B: language authority, unsupported transformations, accepted control behavior; one commit.
s13: Pressure with the pinned Graph3D saddle frontend through the existing gallery router; risk High; B + V: trace, camera/topology pins, actual host; reject unrepresented edits; one commit.
s14: Check supply-tax/Graph2D capability reporting and preserve its current source/publication path; risk Medium; B: parameter/fact coherence and existing production route; one commit.
s15: Finalize per-task preview and projection capability reports from these actual callers; risk Medium; S: a route link cannot prove an applied revision; no implied feature parity; one commit.

s16: Verify exact source handoff to existing local edition builders; expose only currently supported publication paths; risk High; B: stale draft, immutable bytes, no-JS output and unsupported-domain gaps; one commit.

s17: Add held-out valid/invalid task cases and request-fulfillment checks separate from compilation success; risk Medium; S: untouched starter fails changed-task intent; editorial truth qualified; one commit.
s18: Harden untrusted invocation boundaries and cross-domain spoofing cases; risk High; B: size/path/read errors, wrong domain/pins, forged result/source, zero fallback; one commit.

s19: Prove narrow frontend entrypoints with two structurally different consumers; retain only measured common plumbing; risk High; B: type/import cost, public-export compatibility, domain evidence retained; one commit.

s20: Retire duplicated mechanics beside migrated callers; preserve legacy command behavior with delegation; risk Medium; B: old/new result parity, no duplicate authority, source graph checks; one commit.

s21: Update the canonical generation routing guide and executable task packet with accepted/rejected examples; risk Low; F: every example executes; supported-input distinctions remain explicit; one commit.

s22: Execute the retained author tasks and record source bytes, files touched, repair steps and specialist interventions; risk Medium; S + V: actual authored outputs, coherent preview/edition, no invented timing; one commit.

s23: Run broad release and supported-browser preservation; repair attributable failures at their owners; risk High; B + V: full tests/build, fixed budgets, R1/R2/R3/tax and selected code/Graph3D checks; one commit.

s24: Record measured benefit, remaining R4 obligations and mathematical-expansion handoff; close receipts and commit; risk Low; F: exact evidence, validated Theseus, clean scoped worktree; one commit.
Brief tracked contexts, no subagents, same port-8000 server, existing domain owners; approved exemplar and promotion policy in source proposal.
disallowedWork: s01 STOP: Conflicting current authority
s02 STOP: Cannot fit without broader redesign or budget waiver
s03 STOP: New universal capability ontology required
s04 STOP: Loss of domain information or new truth owner
s05 STOP: Dynamic plugin loading or user-code execution needed
s06 STOP: Probability grammar expansion
s07 STOP: New algebra or motif required
s08 STOP: Silent change to legacy command meaning
s09 STOP: New host state machine or choreography needed
s10 STOP: Material new visual/editorial decision needs human review before propagation
s11 STOP: General knowledge ontology required
s12 STOP: New language/refactor topology or false publication parity
s13 STOP: New Graph3D content or equation-shaped semantics needed
s14 STOP: Economics migration beyond reporting/preservation
s15 STOP: Requires a new universal host/publication interface
s16 STOP: Browser writes, remote storage or public deployment required
s17 STOP: Requires free-prose automatic grading
s18 STOP: New execution authority or package loader required
s19 STOP: Speculative abstraction or fixed-gate failure cannot be repaired in scope
s20 STOP: Unrelated compatibility migration
s21 STOP: Packet advertises unsupported generation or model success
s22 STOP: Subjective new output needs approval; no live call implied
s23 STOP: Unrelated repairs, unsafe authority or new visual treatment
s24 STOP: Required proof or approved work incomplete
No external model calls, new domains/motifs, universal schema, budget waiver, runtime rewrite, remote/browser writes, deployment, merge or automatic successor.
goal: Supported author tasks use consistent entrypoints while domain evidence, previews and immutable editions remain coherent.
commitCadence: One independently reversible verified slice and its Theseus evidence per commit; no merge.
stopConditions: Stop for material new visual/editorial judgment before propagation, unsafe authority, scope expansion, unavailable required proof, user pause or completed scope. Repair attributable nonvisual failures without waiving fixed gates.
